intro: The In-Person Sensitivity Test checks how you think, observe and communicate, not memorised answers. Speak honestly, give specific examples, and connect everything to your own observations and work.

questions.q: Why do you want to study design?
questions.look: A personal, specific moment that made you curious about design, not 'I love drawing'. Show what kind of problems excite you.

questions.q: Why NID and not another design school?
questions.look: Know NID's approach (learning by doing, studio culture, its history since 1961 and the 1958 India Report by Charles and Ray Eames). Link it to how you like to learn.

questions.q: Tell us about yourself.
questions.look: 60–90 seconds: where you're from, what you notice and make, one thing that makes you different. Not a CV list.

questions.q: What is special about your hometown, from a design point of view?
questions.look: Crafts, architecture, food, festivals, how people use public space. Mention specific details you've observed.

questions.q: What do you do in your free time, and what has it taught you?
questions.look: Connect the hobby to observation, patience, making or people.

questions.q: What is your biggest strength and your biggest weakness as a future designer?
questions.look: An honest weakness with what you're doing about it. Strengths backed by an example.

questions.q: Talk about an object you love. Why is it well designed?
questions.look: Form, material, use, feeling and context. Mention who uses it and how. Handle it in your mind as you talk.

questions.q: Show us something badly designed that you use every day. How would you improve it?
questions.look: A specific problem you've experienced, who suffers from it, and a realistic improvement.

questions.q: Look around this room. What would you change and why?
questions.look: Observe first (light, seating, signage, movement), then suggest changes for the people who use it.

questions.q: Describe the bus stop nearest your home. Who uses it and what are its problems?
questions.look: Users (students, elderly, vendors), times of day, weather, safety. Specific details.

questions.q: Tell us about an Indian craft you know well.
questions.look: Where it's from, material, process, who makes it, and the challenges it faces today. Karnataka crafts are a strong choice.

questions.q: How can design help traditional crafts survive?
questions.look: Respect for the craftsperson; new products/markets without losing the essence; fair pay; storytelling.

questions.q: Name a designer or design you admire and explain why.
questions.look: Know the work properly; say what you learned from it, not just that it's famous.

questions.q: What does sustainable design mean to you?
questions.look: Materials, life cycle, repair, local resources; examples from Indian everyday life (steel tiffins, banana leaves, repair culture).

questions.q: Will AI replace designers?
questions.look: A balanced view: AI as a tool; designers bring empathy, judgement, context and responsibility.

questions.q: How would you make a public space more inclusive?
questions.look: Specific users (wheelchair users, elderly, children, visually impaired), specific changes, and why they help everyone.

questions.q: What makes a design 'good'?
questions.look: Usefulness, clarity, beauty, honesty to material, longevity, fit for the user and context. Give an example.

questions.q: Explain the model you made in the studio test.
questions.look: What you understood from the brief → your idea → why these materials → what you'd improve. Calm and structured.

questions.q: Which of your works are you proudest of, and why?
questions.look: The thinking behind it and what you learned, not just that it looks nice.

questions.q: Tell us about something you made that failed. What did you learn?
questions.look: Honesty, reflection and what you changed afterwards.

questions.q: Describe a time you worked in a team. What was your role?
questions.look: Listening, contributing and handling disagreement, with a specific example.

questions.q: Which question in the Prelims did you enjoy most and why?
questions.look: Recall your approach and what you'd do differently. Shows reflection.

questions.q: Which design discipline interests you most and why?
questions.look: Know the difference between product, communication, textile, ceramics, animation etc. Connect to your interests.

questions.q: Where do you see yourself in ten years?
questions.look: A direction and values, not a fixed job title. Who you want to design for.

questions.q: Which problem in India would you most like to solve through design?
questions.look: A real problem you've observed, who it affects, and the first step you'd take.

questions.q: What do your parents think about you choosing design?
questions.look: Honest and positive; show you've thought about the career seriously.

questions.q: If you could redesign one thing about your school, what would it be?
questions.look: Specific, observed, with users in mind.

questions.q: Describe the colour of your morning.
questions.look: Imagination and sensitivity: tie colours to moments, light, sounds and feelings.

questions.q: Here is a paper clip. Tell us 5 things it could be.
questions.look: Fluency and originality; think aloud; move beyond the obvious quickly.

questions.q: What did you notice on your way here today?
questions.look: Observation habit. Prepare by actually noticing on the day of the interview.
